title: A volatile counter shared with an ISR
description: A 1 kHz interrupt increments a volatile uint32_t counter while a foreground task reads and resets it. Is this safe? Explain the distinct roles of compiler visibility, indivisible accesses, and synchronization. Propose a design and state what target-specific facts you need.
prompt: A 1 kHz interrupt increments a volatile uint32_t counter while a foreground task reads and resets it. Is this safe? Explain the distinct roles of compiler visibility, indivisible accesses, and synchronization. Propose a design and state what target-specific facts you need.
constraints: State assumptions and separate measurements from guarantees.
rubric: Do not assume volatile creates an atomic read-modify-write.
Discuss a bounded critical section or suitable lock-free atomic operation and ISR constraints.
follow_ups: What changes for a 64-bit counter on a 32-bit MCU?
Can disabling interrupts on one core protect against a second core?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
